articles.title: 完形填空 · 把写作真正放到优先级上
articles.context: 文章引用作家Harlan Coben的观点：写作应像普通工作一样被认真安排，真正想写的人需要牺牲部分娱乐、重新排序时间，但阅读仍不可放弃。
rows: Harlan Coben believes that if you're a writer, you'll find the time; and that if you can't find the time, then writing isn't a priority and you're not a writer.
哈兰·科本认为，如果你真是作家，你就会找到时间；如果找不到时间，那说明写作并非优先事项，你也不能算真正的作家。
advance
For him, writing is a normal job—a job like any other.
对他而言，写作就是一份普通工作，和其他工作没有本质区别。
explain
He has compared it with plumbing, pointing out that a plumber doesn't wake up and say that he can't work with pipes today.
他把写作比作水管工的工作：水管工不会一觉醒来就说自己今天没法和管道打交道。
compare
If, like most writers these days, you're holding down a job to pay the bills, it's not easy to find the time to write.
如果你像如今大多数写作者一样，还要靠一份工作支付账单，那么挤出写作时间并不容易。
qualify
But it's not impossible.
但这并非不可能。
contrast
It requires determination and single-mindedness.
它需要决心和专注。
emphasize
Remember that most bestselling authors began writing when they were doing other things to earn a living.
要记住，大多数畅销书作家开始写作时，也在做别的事情谋生。
encourage
And today, even writers who are fairly well-known often have to do other work to supplement their writing income.
即使在今天，颇有名气的作家也常常要做其他工作，补充写作收入。
report
As Harlan Coben has suggested, it's a question of priorities.
正如哈兰·科本所说，这归根到底是优先级的问题。
conclude
To make writing a priority, you'll have to sacrifice some of your day-to-day activities and some things you really enjoy.
要让写作成为优先事项，你就得牺牲一些日常活动，以及一些真正喜欢做的事情。
warning
Depending on your interests and your lifestyle, that might mean spending less time watching television or listening to music, though some people can write while they listen to music.
根据你的兴趣和生活方式，这可能意味着少看电视、少听音乐，当然也有人能一边听音乐一边写作。
example
You might have to cut down on the amount of exercise or sport you do.
你也许还得减少锻炼或运动的时间。
example
You'll have to make social media an occasional activity rather than a daily, time-consuming habit.
你需要把社交媒体变成偶尔进行的活动，而不是每天耗费大量时间的习惯。
warning
There'll probably have to be less socialising with your friends and less time with your family.
你可能不得不少和朋友社交，也少花一些时间陪家人。
warning
It's a tough learning curve and it won't always make you popular.
这是一个艰难的适应过程，而且未必总能让别人满意。
qualify
There's just one thing you should try to keep at least some time for, in addition to your writing—and that's reading.
不过，除了写作之外，有一件事你至少应该保留一些时间去做，那就是阅读。
advance
Any writer needs to read as much and as widely as they can; it's the one indispensable supporter—something you can't do without.
任何写作者都应尽可能多读、广泛读；阅读是不可或缺的支撑，是绝不能缺少的东西。
emphasize
Time is finite.
时间是有限的。
emphasize
The older you get, the quicker it seems to go.
年纪越大，越会觉得时间流逝得更快。
compare
We need to use it as carefully and as productively as we can, that means prioritising our activities so that we spend most time on the things we really want to do.
我们需要尽可能谨慎而高效地使用时间，这意味着给活动排出优先级，把最多时间花在自己真正想做的事情上。
conclude
If you're a writer, that means—above all—writing.
如果你是写作者，那么最重要的当然就是写作。
conclude

articles.title: 阅读 Text 1 · “气候友好型鸡蛋”能成为下一类高端食品吗
articles.context: 文章介绍通过再生农业生产的“气候友好型鸡蛋”：利用土壤、覆盖作物与放养体系减碳，并讨论消费者是否愿意为这种可持续属性支付溢价。
rows: On a recent sunny day, 13,000 chickens roam over Larry Brown's 40 windswept acres in Shiner, Texas.
最近一个阳光明媚的日子里，1.3万只鸡在得州夏纳拉里·布朗那40英亩迎风的土地上自由活动。
story
Some rest in the shade of a parked car.
有些鸡在停着的汽车阴影下休息。
story
Others drink water with the cows.
另一些则和奶牛一起喝水。
story
This all seems random, but it's by design, part of what the $6.1 billion U.S. egg industry bets will be its next big thing: climate-friendly eggs.
这一切看似随意，其实都是精心设计的，也是规模61亿美元的美国鸡蛋行业押注的下一件大事：气候友好型鸡蛋。
conclude

These eggs, which are making their debut now on shelves for as much as $8 a dozen, are still labeled organic and animal-friendly, but they're also from birds that live on farms using regenerative agriculture—special techniques to cultivate rich soils that can trap greenhouse gases.
这些鸡蛋刚刚上市，每打售价最高达8美元；它们仍被标为有机、动物友好，但还来自采用再生型农业的农场——这种特殊技术通过培育肥沃土壤来吸收温室气体。
explain
Such eggs could be marketed as helping to fight climate change.
因此，这类鸡蛋可以被宣传为有助于应对气候变化。
conclude
“I'm excited about our progress,” says Brown, who is adding more cover crops that draw worms and crickets for the chickens to eat.
布朗说：“我们的进展让我很兴奋。”他正在增加更多覆盖作物，以吸引蚯蚓和蟋蟀供鸡啄食。
dialogue
The birds' waste then fertilizes fields.
鸡的排泄物随后又为土地施肥。
sequence
Such improvements “allow our hens to forage for higher-quality natural feed that will be good for the land, the hens, and the eggs that we supply to our customers.”
这些改进“让母鸡能够觅食质量更高的天然饲料，这对土地、母鸡以及我们供应给顾客的鸡蛋都有好处”。
dialogue
The egg industry's push is the first major test of whether animal products from regenerative farms can become the next premium offering.
鸡蛋行业的这次推动，是首次大规模检验再生型农场的动物产品能否成为下一类高端商品。
advance
In barely more than a decade, organic eggs went from being dismissed as a niche product in natural foods stores to being sold at Walmart.
短短十多年里，有机鸡蛋从天然食品店里被轻视的小众商品，变成了沃尔玛也销售的产品。
story
More recently there were similar doubts about probiotics and plant-based meats, but both have exploded into major supermarket categories.
更近些时候，人们也曾同样怀疑益生菌和植物肉，但两者后来都迅速成长为超市中的重要品类。
compare
If the sustainable-egg rollout is successful, it could open the floodgates for regenerative beef, broccoli, and beyond.
如果可持续鸡蛋推广成功，就可能为再生型牛肉、西兰花乃至更多产品打开闸门。
conclude

Regenerative products could be a hard sell, because the concept is tough to define quickly, says Julie Stanton, associate professor of agricultural economics at Pennsylvania State University Brandywine.
宾州州立大学布兰迪万校区农业经济学副教授朱莉·斯坦顿说，再生型产品可能不容易卖，因为这个概念很难迅速解释清楚。
qualify
Such farming also brings minimal, if any, improvement to the food products, though some producers say their eggs have more protein.
这种农业方式对食品本身的改善也非常有限，甚至可能没有，尽管一些生产者声称鸡蛋含有更多蛋白质。
qualify
The industry is betting that the same consumers paying more for premium attributes such as free-range, non-GMO, and pasture-raised eggs will embrace sustainability.
行业押注，那些愿意为散养、非转基因、牧场饲养等高端属性多付钱的消费者，也会接受可持续性。
report

Surveys show that younger generations are more concerned about climate change, and some of the success of plant-based meat can be chalked up to shoppers wanting to signal their desire to protect the environment.
调查显示，年轻一代更关注气候变化；植物肉的一部分成功，也可归因于消费者希望通过购买行为表达保护环境的愿望。
report
Young adults “really care about the planet,” says John Brunnquell, president of Egg Innovations.
Egg Innovations公司总裁约翰·布伦奎尔说，年轻人“真的很关心这个星球”。
dialogue
“They are absolutely altering the food chain beyond what I think even they understand what they're doing.”
“他们确实正在改变食物链，改变的程度甚至超出了他们自己对所做之事的理解。”
dialogue

articles.title: 阅读 Text 2 · 为什么越来越多美国人选择“退休后继续工作”
articles.context: 文章介绍美国“非退休”趋势：寿命延长、心理满足与财务压力共同推动越来越多人退休后继续工作，同时也提醒人们提前规划长期财务目标。
rows: More Americans are opting to work well into retirement, a growing trend that threatens to upend the old workforce model.
越来越多美国人选择退休后继续工作，这一趋势正在挑战传统劳动力模式。
advance
One in three Americans who are at least 40 have, or plan to have a job in retirement to prepare for a longer life, according to a survey conducted by Harris Poll for TD Ameritrade.
哈里斯民调为德美利证券所做的调查显示，40岁及以上美国人中，每三人就有一人已经或计划退休后继续工作，以应对更长寿命。
statistic

Even more surprising is that more than half of “unretirees”—those who plan to work in retirement or went back to work after retiring—said they would be employed in their later years even if they had enough money to settle down, the survey showed.
更令人意外的是，超过一半的“非退休者”——即计划退休后工作或退休后重返职场的人——表示，即使有足够的钱安度晚年，他们晚年仍会工作。
statistic
Financial needs aren't the only culprit for the “unretirement” trend.
财务需求并不是“非退休”趋势的唯一原因。
contrast
Other reasons, according to the study, include personal fulfillment such as staying mentally fit, preventing boredom or avoiding depression.
研究显示，其他原因还包括个人满足感，例如保持头脑活跃、避免无聊或预防抑郁。
explain
“The concept of retirement is evolving,” said Christine Russell, senior manager of retirement at TD Ameritrade.
德美利证券退休业务高级经理克里斯蒂娜·拉塞尔说：“退休的概念正在变化。”
dialogue
“It's not just about finances.
“它不只是财务问题。
dialogue
The value of work is also driving folks to continue working past retirement.”
工作的价值本身，也在推动人们退休后继续工作。”
dialogue
One reason for the change in retirement patterns: Americans are living longer.
退休模式变化的一个原因，是美国人活得更久。
advance
Older Americans are also the fastest-growing segment of the U.S. workforce.
老年美国人也是美国劳动力中增长最快的群体。
report
The percentage of retirement-age people in the labor force has doubled over the past three decades.
过去30年，达到退休年龄却仍在劳动力中的人口比例翻了一番。
statistic
About 20% of people 65 and older were in the workforce in February 2019, up from an all-time low of 10% in January 1985, according to money manager United Income.
资产管理机构United Income数据显示，2019年2月，65岁及以上人口约20%仍在就业，高于1985年1月历史低点的10%。
statistic
Because of longer life spans, Americans are also boosting their savings to preserve their nest eggs, the TD Ameritrade study showed, which surveyed 2,000 adults between 40 to 79.
德美利证券对2000名40至79岁成年人所做的调查显示，由于寿命延长，美国人也在增加储蓄，以保住养老积蓄。
explain
Six in 10 “unretirees” are increasing their savings in anticipation of a longer life.
十个“非退休者”中有六个正在增加储蓄，以应对更长寿命。
statistic
Among the most popular ways they are doing this, the company said, is by reducing their overall expenses, securing life insurance or maximizing their contributions to retirement accounts.
该公司称，最常见的做法包括减少总体开支、购买人寿保险，或尽可能提高退休账户缴款。
report

Unfortunately, many people who are opting to work in retirement are preparing to do so because they are worried about making ends meet in their later years, said Brent Weiss, a co-founder at Baltimore-based financial-planning firm Facet Wealth.
巴尔的摩理财公司Facet Wealth联合创始人布伦特·韦斯说，遗憾的是，许多人之所以准备退休后继续工作，是因为担心晚年收支难以平衡。
warning
He suggested that preretirees should speak with a financial adviser to set long-term financial goals.
他建议临近退休者与财务顾问沟通，设定长期财务目标。
encourage
“The most challenging moments in life are getting married, starting a family and ultimately retiring,” Weiss said.
韦斯说：“人生最具挑战的时刻包括结婚、组建家庭以及最终退休。”
dialogue
“It's not just a financial decision, but an emotional one.
“这不只是一个财务决定，也是一个情感决定。
dialogue
Many people believe they can't retire.”
许多人认为自己根本退不了休。”
dialogue

articles.title: 阅读 Text 3 · 数字产品里的“暗黑模式”如何操纵用户
articles.context: 文章解释数字界面的“暗黑模式”：通过隐藏成本、误导流程、退出困难等设计影响用户决策，并呼吁企业内部协作、自律及监管共同减少数字欺骗。
rows: We have all encountered them, in both our personal and professional lives.
无论私人生活还是工作中，我们都遇到过这类情况。
advance
Think about the times you felt tricked or frustrated by a membership or subscription that had a seamless sign-up process but was later difficult to cancel.
想想那些会员或订阅：注册时无比顺畅，取消时却异常困难，让你感到受骗或挫败。
example
Something that should be simple and transparent can be complicated, intentionally or unintentionally, in ways that impair consumer choice.
原本应当简单透明的事情，可能被有意或无意地复杂化，从而损害消费者的选择。
warning
These are examples of dark patterns.
这些就是“暗黑模式”的例子。
conclude
First coined in 2010 by user experience expert Harry Brignull, “dark patterns” is a catch-all term for practices that manipulate user interfaces to influence the decision-making ability of users.
“暗黑模式”一词由用户体验专家哈里·布里格纳尔于2010年首次提出，是对一类做法的统称：它们通过操纵用户界面来影响用户的决策能力。
explain

Brignull identifies 12 types of common dark patterns, ranging from misdirection and hidden costs to “roach motel,” where a user experience seems easy and intuitive at the start, but turns difficult when the user tries to get out.
布里格纳尔总结了12种常见暗黑模式，从误导、隐藏成本到“蟑螂旅馆”式设计——进入时看似轻松直觉，想退出时却困难重重。
explain
In a 2019 study of 53,000 product pages and 11,000 websites, researchers found that about one in 10 employs these design practices.
2019年一项覆盖5.3万个产品页面和1.1万个网站的研究发现，大约十分之一使用了这些设计手法。
statistic
Though widely prevalent, the concept of dark patterns is still not well understood.
尽管暗黑模式十分普遍，人们对这一概念仍缺乏充分理解。
contrast
Business and nonprofit leaders should be aware of dark patterns and try to avoid the gray areas they engender.
企业和非营利组织领导者应了解暗黑模式，并努力避免它们造成的灰色地带。
encourage
Where is the line between ethical, persuasive design and dark patterns?
合乎伦理的说服性设计与暗黑模式之间，界线究竟在哪里？
ask

Businesses should engage in conversations with IT, compliance, risk, and legal teams to review their privacy policy, and include in the discussion the customer/user experience designers and coders responsible for the company's user interface, as well as the marketers and advertisers responsible for sign-ups, checkout baskets, pricing, and promotions.
企业应与IT、合规、风险和法律团队沟通，审查隐私政策；同时还应让负责用户界面的客户/用户体验设计师和程序员，以及负责注册、购物车、定价和促销的营销与广告人员加入讨论。
encourage
Any or all these teams can play a role in creating or avoiding “digital deception.”
这些团队中的任何一个或全部，都可能参与制造或避免“数字欺骗”。
conclude
Lawmakers and regulators are slowly starting to address the ambiguity around dark patterns, most recently at the state level.
立法者和监管者正逐步处理暗黑模式周围的模糊性，最近的行动主要发生在州一级。
advance

In March, the California Attorney General announced the approval of additional regulations under the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) that “ensure that consumers will not be confused or misled when seeking to exercise their data privacy rights.”
3月，加州总检察长宣布批准《加州消费者隐私法》下的补充规定，以“确保消费者在行使数据隐私权时不会受到迷惑或误导”。
report

The regulations aim to ban dark patterns—this means prohibiting companies from using confusing language or unnecessary steps such as forcing them to click through multiple screens or listen to reasons why they shouldn't opt out.
这些规定旨在禁止暗黑模式，也就是禁止企业使用令人困惑的语言或不必要步骤，比如强迫消费者点击多个页面，或听取为何不应退出的理由。
explain
As more states consider promulgating additional regulations, there is a need for greater accountability from within the business community.
随着更多州考虑制定补充规定，商业界内部需要承担更大的问责责任。
warning

Dark patterns also can be addressed on a self-regulatory basis, but only if organizations hold themselves accountable, not just to legal requirements but also to industry best practices and standards.
暗黑模式也可以通过行业自律来应对，但前提是组织真正对自己负责，不只满足法律要求，也遵守行业最佳实践和标准。
conclude

articles.title: 阅读 Text 4 · 一堂伦理课真的能改变吃肉行为吗
articles.context: 文章介绍现实情境中的伦理教育实验：讨论工厂化养殖伦理的学生随后肉类购买下降，研究者认为社会影响、视频情绪作用与理性论证可能共同作用，但因果机制仍不确定。
rows: Although ethics classes are common around the world, scientists are unsure if their lessons can actually change behavior; evidence either way is weak, relying on contrived laboratory tests or sometimes unreliable self-reports.
虽然伦理课在世界各地都很常见，但科学家并不确定课程能否真正改变行为；支持或反对的证据都很薄弱，因为往往依赖人为设计的实验室测试或有时并不可靠的自我报告。
qualify
But a new study published in Cognition found that, in at least one real-world situation, a single ethics lesson may have had lasting effects.
但发表在《认知》上的一项新研究发现，至少在一个真实情境中，一堂伦理课可能产生了持续影响。
contrast
The researchers investigated one class session's impact on eating meat.
研究人员考察了一堂课对吃肉行为的影响。
advance

They chose this particular behavior for three reasons, according to study co-author Eric Schwitzgebel, a philosopher at the University of California, Riverside: students' attitudes on the topic are variable and unstable, behavior is easily measurable, and ethics literature largely agrees that eating less meat is good because it reduces environmental harm and animal suffering.
研究共同作者、加州大学河滨分校哲学家埃里克·施维茨格贝尔说，选择这一行为有三个原因：学生对吃肉的态度容易变化且不稳定；行为容易测量；伦理学文献普遍认为少吃肉有益，因为能减少环境损害和动物痛苦。
explain
Half of the students in four large philosophy classes read an article on the ethics of factory-farmed meat, optionally watched an 11-minute video on the topic and joined a 50-minute discussion.
四个大型哲学班中，一半学生阅读了关于工厂化养殖肉类伦理的文章，可选择观看一段11分钟视频，并参加50分钟讨论。
sequence
The other half focused on charitable giving instead.
另一半学生则讨论慈善捐赠。
contrast
Then, unknown to the students, the researchers studied their anonymized meal-card purchases for that semester—nearly 14,000 receipts for almost 500 students.
随后，在学生不知情的情况下，研究人员分析了他们当学期匿名化的餐卡购买记录——近500名学生、约1.4万张小票。
sequence

Schwitzgebel predicted the intervention would have no effect; he had previously found that ethics professors do not differ from other professors on a range of behaviors, including voting rates, blood donation and returning library books.
施维茨格贝尔原本预测干预不会有效，因为他此前发现，伦理学教授在投票率、献血、归还图书等一系列行为上并不比其他教授不同。
report
But among student subjects who discussed meat ethics, meal purchases containing meat decreased from 52 to 45 percent—and this effect held steady for the study's duration of several weeks.
但在讨论肉类伦理的学生中，含肉餐食的购买比例从52%降到45%，而且这一效果在持续数周的研究期内保持稳定。
contrast
Purchases from the other group remained at 52 percent.
另一组的购买比例仍为52%。
statistic
“That's actually a pretty large effect for a pretty small intervention,” Schwitzgebel says.
施维茨格贝尔说：“对于这样一个很小的干预而言，这其实是相当大的效果。”
dialogue
Psychologist Nina Strohminger at the University of Pennsylvania, who was not involved in the study, says she wants the effect to be real but cannot rule out some unknown confounding variable.
未参与研究的宾夕法尼亚大学心理学家妮娜·斯特罗明格表示，她希望这个效果是真的，但无法排除某个未知混杂变量。
qualify
And if real, she notes, it might be reversible by another nudge: “Easy come, easy go.”
她还指出，即使效果真实，也可能被另一次轻微推动逆转：“来得容易，去得也快。”
warning

Schwitzgebel suspects the greatest impact came from social influence—classmates or teaching assistants leading the discussions may have shared their own vegetarianism, showing it as achievable or more common.
施维茨格贝尔怀疑，最大影响来自社会影响：同学或主持讨论的助教可能分享了自己的素食习惯，让素食看起来更可实现、也更常见。
explain
Second, the video may have had an emotional impact.
第二，视频可能产生了情绪影响。
sequence
Least rousing, he thinks, was rational argument, although his co-authors say reason might play a bigger role.
他认为最不具煽动力的是理性论证，不过共同作者认为理性可能发挥了更大作用。
qualify
Now the researchers are probing the specific effects of teaching style, teaching assistants' eating habits and students' video exposure.
目前，研究人员正在进一步考察教学风格、助教饮食习惯以及学生观看视频的具体影响。
report
Meanwhile, Schwitzgebel—who had predicted no effect—will be eating his words.
与此同时，曾预测“不会有效”的施维茨格贝尔看来不得不收回自己的话。
playful

articles.title: 阅读 Part B · 中断后如何安全恢复运动
articles.context: 文章提供恢复运动的五条策略：降低起点、倾听身体、建立习惯、先练动作、与他人一起运动，在避免受伤和倦怠的同时逐步恢复体能。
rows: Getting back into exercise after a break can be a challenge in the best of times, but with gyms and in-person exercise classes off-limits to many people these days, it can be tricky to know where to start.
中断一段时间后重新运动，即使在正常时期也有挑战；如今许多人又无法去健身房或参加线下课程，更容易不知道从哪里开始。
advance
And it's important to get the right dose of activity.
而且，掌握合适的运动量非常重要。
emphasize
“Too much too soon either results in injury or burnout,” says Mary Yoke, PhD, a faculty member in the kinesiology department at Indiana University in Bloomington.
印第安纳大学布卢明顿分校运动机能学教师玛丽·约克说：“太多、太快，只会导致受伤或倦怠。”
dialogue
The following simple strategies will help you return to exercise safely after a break.
下面这些简单策略能帮助你在中断后安全恢复运动。
advance
Don't try to go back to what you were doing before your break.
不要一开始就恢复到中断前的运动量。
warning

If you were walking 3 miles a day, playing 18 holes of golf three times a week, or lifting 10-pound dumbbells for three sets of 10 reps, reduce activity to half a mile every other day, or nine holes of golf once a week with short walks on other days, or use 5-pound dumbbells for one set of 10 reps.
如果以前每天走3英里、每周三次打18洞高尔夫，或用10磅哑铃做三组每组10次，那么现在可以改为隔天走半英里、每周一次打9洞并在其他日子短走，或用5磅哑铃做一组10次。
example
Increase time, distance, and intensity gradually.
时间、距离和强度都要逐步增加。
encourage

“This isn't something you can do overnight,” says Keri L. Denay, MD, lead author of a recent American College of Sports Medicine advisory that encourages Americans to not overlook the benefits of activity during the pandemic.
美国运动医学会近期建议的主要作者克里·德奈医生说：“这不是一夜之间能做到的事。”该建议提醒美国人不要忽视疫情期间运动的好处。
dialogue
But you'll reap benefits such as less anxiety and improved sleep right away.
不过，你很快就能收获焦虑减少、睡眠改善等好处。
conclude
If you're breathing too hard to talk in complete sentences, back off.
如果喘得连完整句子都说不出来，就降低强度。
warning
If you feel good, go a little longer or faster.
如果感觉不错，可以稍微延长时间或加快速度。
encourage
Feeling wiped out after a session?
一次训练后筋疲力尽？
ask
Go easier next time.
那下次就轻松一点。
resolve
And stay alert to serious symptoms, such as chest pain or pressure, severe shortness of breath or dizziness, or faintness, and seek medical attention immediately.
同时警惕胸痛或压迫感、严重呼吸困难、眩晕或昏厥等严重症状，并立即就医。
warning
Consistency is the key to getting stronger and building endurance and stamina.
坚持是增强力量、建立耐力和体能的关键。
emphasize
Ten minutes of activity per day is a good start, says Marcus Jackovitz, DPT, a physical therapist at the University of Miami Hospital.
迈阿密大学医院物理治疗师马库斯·杰科维茨说，每天活动10分钟就是很好的起点。
report
All the experts we spoke with highly recommend walking because it's the easiest, most accessible form of exercise.
我们采访的所有专家都强烈推荐步行，因为它是最简单、最容易做到的运动形式。
report
Although it can be a workout on its own, if your goal is to get back to Zumba classes, tennis, cycling, or any other activity, walking is also a great first step.
步行本身可以作为锻炼；如果你的目标是恢复尊巴、网球、骑行或其他运动，它也是极好的第一步。
conclude
Even if you can't yet do a favorite activity, you can practice the moves.
即使暂时不能真正进行最喜欢的运动，也可以先练习动作。
encourage
With or without a club or racket, swing like you're hitting the ball.
无论手里有没有球杆或球拍，都可以模仿击球动作。
example
Paddle like you're in a kayak or canoe.
像坐在皮划艇或独木舟里一样练习划桨。
example
Mimic your favorite swimming strokes.
模仿你最喜欢的游泳动作。
example
The action will remind you of the joy the activity brought you and prime your muscles for when you can get out there again.
这些动作会唤起运动曾带给你的快乐，也会提前让肌肉为重新上场做好准备。
conclude
Exercising with others “can keep you accountable and make it more fun, so you're more likely to do it again,” Jackovitz says.
杰科维茨说，与别人一起锻炼“能让你更有责任感，也更有趣，因此更可能再次去做”。
dialogue
You can do activities such as golf and tennis or take a walk with others and still be socially distant.
你可以和别人一起打高尔夫、网球或散步，同时仍保持社交距离。
example
But when you can't connect in person, consider using technology.
如果无法线下见面，可以考虑借助技术。
contrast
Chat on the phone with a friend while you walk around your neighborhood.
在社区散步时和朋友打电话聊天。
encourage
FaceTime with a relative as you strength train or stretch at home.
在家做力量训练或拉伸时，可以和亲人视频通话。
encourage
You can also join a livestream or on-demand exercise class.
你还可以参加直播或点播健身课程。
conclude

articles.title: 翻译 · 绘画中的意外结果如何训练创造性解决问题
articles.context: 文章指出，绘画结果偏离预期虽然令人失望，却能训练人适应变化、处理挫折并寻找创造性解决方案，这种能力也可迁移到日常生活。
rows: Although we try our best, sometimes our paintings rarely turn out as originally planned.
尽管我们已经竭尽全力，有时画作仍很少会完全按照最初计划呈现。
qualify

Changes in the light, the limitations of your painting materials, and the lack of experience and technique mean that what you start out trying to achieve may not come to life the way that you expected.
光线变化、绘画材料的限制以及经验和技巧不足，都意味着你最初想实现的效果未必会如预期那样呈现。
explain
Although this can be frustrating and disappointing, it turns out that this can actually be good for you.
虽然这可能令人沮丧、令人失望，但事实证明，它其实可能对你有好处。
contrast
Unexpected results have two benefits: you pretty quickly learn to deal with disappointment and realise that when one door closes, another opens.
意外结果有两个好处：你会很快学会面对失望，并意识到一扇门关上时，另一扇门会打开。
explain
You also quickly learn to adapt and come up with creative solutions to the problems the painting presents, and thinking outside the box will become your second nature.
你也会很快学会适应，并为绘画带来的问题想出创造性解决方案；跳出框架思考最终会成为你的第二天性。
advance
In fact, creative problem-solving skills are incredibly useful in daily life, with which you're more likely to be able to find a solution when a problem arises.
事实上，创造性解决问题的能力在日常生活中极其有用；拥有这种能力，问题出现时你更可能找到解决办法。
conclude
